**Another hadith on its virtue:** Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad [al-Dhuhli] narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Amr informed us, from Ibn Abi Hilal, that Abu al-Rijal Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to him, from his mother 'Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman (who was in the care of 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ), from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet ﷺ sent a man as commander of a expedition (sariyyah), and he used to recite for his companions in their prayers, and he would end with ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ When they returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Ask him why he does that." So they asked him, and he said: "Because it is the attribute of the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Inform him that Allah, the Exalted, loves him."

Al-Bukhari narrated it thus in his book "al-Tawhid." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7375.] Some people omit the mention of "Muhammad al-Dhuhli" and make it from his narration from Ahmad ibn Salih. Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Wahb, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, with this. [Sahih Muslim, no. 813, and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/170).]

**Another hadith:** Al-Bukhari said in the Book of Prayer: "'Ubayd Allah [in A: "Abd Allah"] narrated from Thabit, from Anas, who said: A man from the Ansar used to lead them in prayer at the Mosque of Quba. Whenever he began a surah he would recite to them in the prayer, of what he recited, he would begin with ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ until he finished it, then he would recite another surah with it, and he would do this in every rak'ah. His companions spoke to him and said: 'You begin with this surah, then you do not seem to think it suffices you until you recite another with it. Either recite it, or leave it and recite another.' He said: 'I will not leave it. If you wish me to lead you with it, I will do so, and if you dislike it, I will leave you.' They thought he was among the best of them, and they disliked that anyone other than him should lead them. When the Prophet ﷺ came to them, they informed him of the matter. He said: 'O so-and-so, what prevents you from doing what your companions command you, and what compels you to persist in this surah in every rak'ah?' He said: 'I love it.' He said: 'Your love for it has admitted you into Paradise.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 774.]

Thus al-Bukhari narrated it as a mu'allaq (a hadith cited without its full chain), stated with certainty. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Jami', from al-Bukhari, from Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, and he mentioned it with its chain, the same, identically. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2901.] Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (singular) from the hadith of Ubayd Allah, from Thabit." He said: "Mubarak ibn Fadalah also narrated from Thabit, from Anas, that a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I love this surah: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾' He said: 'Indeed your love for it has admitted you into Paradise.'"

What al-Tirmidhi cited without a chain, Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad as connected (muttasil), so he said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I love this surah: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your love for it [in M: "Indeed your love"] has admitted you into Paradise." [Al-Musnad (3/141).]

**A hadith on its being equal to a third of the Qur'an:** Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il narrated to us, Malik narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah, from his father, from Abu Sa'id, that a man heard another man reciting ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ repeatedly. When morning came, he went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, as though the man belittled it. The Prophet ﷺ [in M: "the Messenger of Allah"] said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is indeed equal to a third of the Qur'an." Isma'il ibn Ja'far added, from Malik, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah, from his father, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "My brother Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man informed me, from the Prophet ﷺ." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7374.]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf and al-Qa'nabi. Abu Dawud narrated it from al-Qa'nabi, and al-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, all from Malik, with this chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 5013 and 6643; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1461; and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/171).] The hadith of Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man was also recorded by al-Nasa'i through two routes, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Malik, with this chain. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. 8029 and 10536.]

**Another hadith:** Al-Bukhari said: Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Ibrahim and al-Dahhak al-Mashriqi narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: "Is one of you unable to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night?" That was difficult for them, and they said: "Which of us can manage that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Allah, the One, the Samad, is a third of the Qur'an." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5015.]

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Nakha'i and al-Dahhak ibn Shurahbil al-Hamdani al-Mashriqi, both from Abu Sa'id. Al-Qarabiri said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim, the scribe of Abu Abd Allah [al-Bukhari], say: Abu Abd Allah al-Bukhari said: "From Ibrahim it is mursal (its link is broken), and from al-Dahhak it is musnad (connected)." [Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (9/60): "The meaning is that the narration of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i from Abu Sa'id is munqati' (broken), and al-Dahhak's narration from him is muttasil (connected)."]

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man spent the whole night reciting ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾. This was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is equal to half of the Qur'an, or a third of it." [Al-Musnad (3/15).]

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Huyayy ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, that Abu Ayyub al-Ansari was in a gathering, saying: "Is none of you able to stand in prayer for a third of the Qur'an every night?" They said: "Is anyone able to do that?" He said: "Indeed, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ is a third of the Qur'an." Then the Prophet ﷺ came while he was listening to Abu Ayyub, and he said: "Abu Ayyub has spoken the truth." [Al-Musnad (2/173).]

**Another hadith:** Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yazid ibn Kaysan narrated to us, Abu Hazim informed me, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Gather together, for I will recite to you a third of the Qur'an." So whoever gathered gathered, then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out and recited ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, then went back in. Some of us said to others: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I will recite to you a third of the Qur'an.' I think this is news that came from heaven." Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out and said: "I said: 'I will recite to you a third of the Qur'an.' Indeed, it [this surah] is equal to a third of the Qur'an."

Muslim narrated it likewise in his Sahih, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, with this chain. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2900, and Sahih Muslim, no. 812.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib." The name of Abu Hazim is Salman.

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Za'idah ibn Qudamah, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym [in A: "ibn Khaythum"], from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from a woman of the Ansar, from Abu Ayyub, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Is one of you unable to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night? For whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ in a night, has indeed recited a third of the Qur'an that night."

This is a hadith with a nine-narrator chain (tusa'i al-isnad) from Imam Ahmad. It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, both from Muhammad ibn Bashshar Bundar (in one manuscript: "Yasar"). Al-Tirmidhi added Qutayba, and both of them narrated it from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, with it. Thus it becomes a ten-narrator chain (ushari) for the two of them. In al-Tirmidhi's narration it reads: "from the wife of Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ayyub," with it [and he graded it hasan]. Then he said: "And on this subject there are reports from Abu al-Darda', Abu Sa'id, Qatada ibn al-Nu'man, Abu Hurayra, Anas, Ibn Umar and Abu Mas'ud." He said: "This is a hasan (sound-good) hadith, and we do not know anyone who narrated this hadith better than the narration of Za'ida." Israil and al-Fudayl ibn Iyad followed him in his narration. Shu'ba and others of the trustworthy narrators related this hadith from Mansur, and they disagreed about it (idtarabu fihi).

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, or a man from the Ansar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ has recited a third of the Qur'an." [Musnad, 5/141.]

Al-Nasa'i related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla," from the hadith of Hushaym, from Husayn, from Ibn Abi Layla, with it. But in his narration the name Hilal ibn Yasaf does not appear. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10521.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Qays [in one manuscript: "Ishaq"], from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abu Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an." [Musnad, 4/122.]

Ibn Majah related it in the same way, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi, from Waki, with it. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3789.] Al-Nasa'i related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla" from various other routes, from Amr ibn Maymun, both as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) and as a mawquf (ending with a companion). [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra nos. 10529, 10525, 10528.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Bahz narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Abi al-Samit narrated to us [in one manuscript: "Bakr ibn Abi al-Simt"], Qatada narrated to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talha, from Abu al-Darda', that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Is one of you incapable of reciting a third of the Qur'an every day?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are weaker than that and less able." He said: "Indeed Allah divided the Qur'an into three parts, and ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ is a third of the Qur'an." [Musnad, 1/447; Sahih Muslim no. 811; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10537.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Umayya ibn Khalid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muslim, the nephew of Ibn Shihab, narrated to us, from his paternal uncle al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, who is Ibn Awf, from his mother, who was Umm Kulthum bint Uqba [in one manuscript: "Utba"] ibn Abi Mu'ayt, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an."

Likewise al-Nasa'i related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla," from Amr ibn Ali, from Umayya ibn Khalid, with it. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10531.] Then he related it through the route of Malik, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, as his own statement (qawlahu, i.e., not traced to the Prophet ﷺ). [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10533.] Al-Nasa'i also related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla" from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Harith ibn al-Fudayl al-Ansari, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman: that a group of the companions of Muhammad ﷺ told him from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an for whoever prays with it." [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10532.]

Another hadith on the reward of reciting it bringing Paradise: Imam Malik ibn Anas said, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ubayd ibn Hunayn, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: "I came along with the Prophet ﷺ, and he heard a man reciting ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Wajabat' (it is obligatory)." I said: "And what is obligatory?" He said: "Paradise." [Muwatta, 2/208; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2897; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 2/171.]

Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Malik. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib (a sound-good hadith that is also gharib, meaning transmitted through a single route); we do not know it except from the hadith of Malik."

And the hadith previously mentioned has already passed: "Your love for it has caused you to enter Paradise."

A hadith on repeating its recitation: The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Qutan ibn Nusayr narrated to us, Isa ibn Maymun al-Qurashi narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqashi narrated to us, from Anas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Can none of you manage to recite ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ three times in a night? For indeed it equals a third of the Qur'an." [Musnad Abi Ya'la, 8/150. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/147): "In its chain is Ubays, who is matruk (abandoned)."]

This chain is weak. A better one than it is another hadith. Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad said:

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from Usayd ibn Abi Usayd, from Mu'adh ibn Abd Allah ibn Khubayb, from his father, who said: A heavy rain and darkness afflicted us, so we waited for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to lead us in prayer. He came out, took my hand, and said: "Say." I was silent. He said: "Say." I said: "What should I say?" He said: "Say ﴿He is Allah, the One﴾ and the two protectors (al-Mu'awwidhatayn), when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, three times, and they will suffice you every day twice."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, with it. [Zawa'id al-Musnad, 5/312; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 5082; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3575; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 8/250.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib from this route." Al-Nasa'i related it through another route, from Mu'adh ibn Abd Allah ibn Khubayb, from his father, from Uqba ibn Amir, and mentioned it [with its wording: "it will suffice you for everything"]. [Sunan al-Nasa'i, 8/251.]

Another hadith on the same subject: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, al-Khalil ibn Murra narrated to me, from al-Azhar ibn Abd Allah, from Tamim al-Dari, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah, alone, the One, the Eternal Refuge (Samad), who has not taken a consort or a son, and to whom no one is equal,' ten times, will have written for him forty million good deeds."

Ahmad alone related it. Al-Khalil ibn Murra was declared weak by al-Bukhari and others, in the sense of his being weak in narration (bi-murra).

Another hadith: Ahmad also said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Zabban ibn Fa'id narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ until he finishes it, ten times, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise." Umar said: "Then we will have many, O Messenger of Allah." He ﷺ said: "Allah is greater and better." Ahmad alone related it. [Musnad, 3/437.]

Abu Muhammad al-Darimi related it in his Musnad, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Haywa narrated to us, Abu Uqayl Zahra ibn Ma'bad narrated to us (al-Darimi said: "He was among the abdal (a class of saints)") that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ ten times, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise; whoever recites it twenty times, Allah will build for him two palaces in Paradise; and whoever recites it thirty times, Allah will build for him three palaces in Paradise." Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Then our palaces will be many!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah is wider than that." [Sunan al-Darimi no. 3429.] This is a mursal (a report where the Successor omits the Companion) of good quality.

Another hadith: The hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us, Nuh ibn Qays narrated to me, Muhammad al-Attar informed me, Umm Kathir al-Ansariyya informed me, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ fifty times, Allah will forgive him the sins of fifty years." [Al-Darimi related it in his Sunan no. 3438: Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us in the same wording.] Its chain is weak.

Another hadith: Abu Ya'la said: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites in a day ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ two hundred times, Allah will record for him one thousand five hundred good deeds, unless he has a debt." [Musnad Abi Ya'la, 6/103.] Its chain is weak; Hatim ibn Maymun was declared weak by al-Bukhari and others. al-Tirmidhi related it from Muhammad ibn Marzuq al-Basri, from Hatim ibn Maymun, with it, and its wording is: "Whoever recites every day two hundred times ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, the sins of fifty years will be erased from him, unless he has a debt."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "With this same chain, from the Prophet ﷺ, it is also related that he said: 'Whoever wants to sleep on his bed, and sleeps on his right side, then recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ one hundred times, then on the Day of Resurrection the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will say to him: O My servant, enter Paradise on your right side.'" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2898.] Then he said: "Gharib from the hadith of Thabit, and it has been related through another route from him."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Sahl ibn Bahr narrated to us, Habban ibn Aghlab narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ two hundred times, Allah will remove from him the sins of two hundred years." [Also related by Ibn al-Darис in Fada'il al-Qur'an no. 267, and al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad 6/187, through al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Thabit, with it.] Then he said: "We do not know anyone who related it from Thabit except al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far and al-Aghlab ibn Tamim, and both are close to each other in poor memorization."

Another hadith on supplicating with the names it contains: Al-Nasa'i said, in his explanation of it: Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to me, Abd Allah ibn Buraydah narrated to us, from his father: that he entered the mosque with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there was a man praying and supplicating, saying: "O Allah, I ask You, by my testifying that there is no god but You, the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad), who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, he has asked Him by His Greatest Name, which when He is asked by it He gives, and when He is called upon by it He answers." [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, as in Tuhfat al-Ashraf of al-Mizzi, 2/90.]

It has been related by the rest of the authors of the Sunan through various routes, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, with it. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1493; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3475; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3857.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

Another hadith on reciting it ten times after the obligatory prayer: The hafiz Abu Ya'la [al-Mawsili] [added from one manuscript] said: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Bishr ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Umar ibn Nabhan [in manuscripts M, A and H: "Umar ibn Shaybān"], from Abu Shaddad, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three things, whoever comes with them along with faith, may enter by whichever gate of Paradise he wishes, and be married to the Huris (al-Hur al-'Iyn) wherever he wishes: whoever pardons the one who killed him, pays a hidden debt, and recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ ten times after every obligatory prayer." He said: Abu Bakr said: "Or one of them, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Or one of them." [Musnad Abi Ya'la, 3/332. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/102): "In it is Umar ibn Nabhan, who is matruk."]

A hadith on reciting it upon entering the house: The memorizer of hadith (al-Hafiz) Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sarraj al-'Askari narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Faraj narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Zibriqan narrated to us, from Marwan ibn Salim, from Abu Zur'a ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ when he enters his house, it removes poverty from the people of that house and from the neighbours." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/340).] Its isnad (chain of narration) is weak.

A hadith on frequently reciting it in all circumstances: The memorizer Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Musayyabi narrated to us; Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Tabuk, and the sun rose with a light, a radiance and a brightness such as we had not seen it rise with before. Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and [he] said: 'O Jibril, why do I see the sun rise today with a light, brightness and radiance such as I have not seen it rise with in the past?' He said: 'That is because Mu'awiya ibn Mu'awiya al-Laythi died in Medina today, so Allah sent to him seventy thousand angels who pray over him.' He said: 'And why is that?' He said: 'He used to frequently recite: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, at night and by day, while walking, standing and sitting. Would you like, O Messenger of Allah, that I fold the earth for you so that you may pray over him?' He said: 'Yes.' So he prayed over him."

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi also narrated it in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwa" by way of Yazid ibn Harun, from al-'Ala' Abu Muhammad [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/256) and Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (5/245)]. He is accused of fabrication (wad'), so Allah knows best.

Another route: Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Shami Abu 'Abd Allah narrated to us; 'Uthman ibn al-Haytham, the muezzin of the congregational mosque in Basra (in my presence), narrated to us, from Mahmud Abu 'Abd Allah [in the original manuscript of Musnad Abi Ya'la it reads "Mahmud ibn 'Abd Allah", but here it reads "Mahmud Abi 'Abd Allah", as you see; the correct reading is "Mahbub ibn Hilal", as in the narration of al-Bayhaqi, Allah knows best], from 'Ata' ibn Abi Maymuna, from Anas, who said: Jibril descended upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Mu'awiya ibn Mu'awiya al-Laythi has died; would you like to pray over him?" He said: "Yes." So he struck the earth with his wing, and no tree or hillock remained without being lowered. He raised his bier and looked at him, then he pronounced takbir over him, with behind him two rows of angels, each row seventy thousand angels. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, by what did he attain this rank with Allah, the Exalted?" He said: "By his love for it: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, and his recitation of it while walking, coming, standing and sitting, and in every state." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/258).]

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the narration of 'Uthman ibn al-Haytham the muezzin, from Mahbub ibn Hilal, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Maymuna, from Anas, and so on. This is the correct version [Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (5/246); Ibn al-Durays narrated it in "Fada'il al-Qur'an" under no. 272, by way of Mahbub ibn Hilal; the author cited it in al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya from al-Bayhaqi's narration (5/14) and said: "Munkar from this route"]. Mahbub ibn Hilal: Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: "Not well known" [al-Jarh wa'l-Ta'dil by Ibn Abi Hatim (8/389)]. This has been narrated by other routes, which we have omitted for brevity, and all of them are weak.

Another hadith on its merit together with the two refuges (al-Mu'awwidhatayn): The Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us; Mu'adh ibn Rifa'a narrated to us; 'Ali ibn Yazid narrated to me, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, who said: I met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I took the initiative, took his hand and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by what is the believer saved?" He said: "O 'Uqba, guard your tongue, let your house suffice you, and weep over your sin." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met me again, took the initiative, took my hand and said: "O 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, shall I not teach you the best three surahs revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Great Qur'an?" I said: "Yes, may Allah make me your ransom." He said: He taught me: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, and ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾. Then he said: "O 'Uqba, do not forget them, and do not sleep a night until you have recited them." He said: I have not forgotten them since he said: "Do not forget them," and I have never spent a night without reciting them. 'Uqba said: Then I met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), took the initiative, took his hand and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me of the most virtuous deeds." He said: "O 'Uqba, join ties with the one who cuts you off, give to the one who deprives you, and forgive the one who wrongs you." [Al-Musnad (4/148).]

Al-Tirmidhi narrated part of it in "al-Zuhd", from the hadith of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, and said: "This is a hasan hadith" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2406)]. Its isnad includes 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, 'Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim, all of whom are weak. Ibn Hibban said of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr: "He narrates fabricated reports from reliable narrators, and when he narrates from 'Ali ibn Yazid he brings forth abominations; and when a report's isnad contains 'Ubayd Allah, 'Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim (Abu 'Abd al-Rahman), that report is nothing but what their hands have produced." [Note on the text of Ibn Hibban.] Ahmad narrated it by another route:

Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Usayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khath'ami, from Furwa ibn Mujahid al-Lakhmi, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned the like of it exactly. Ahmad alone narrated it [Al-Musnad (4/158)].

Another hadith on seeking healing with them: Al-Bukhari said: Qutayba narrated to us; al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha, that the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he went to his bed every night, joined his palms, then blew into them and recited in them: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, and ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾; then he would wipe with them as much of his body as he could, beginning with his head and face and what faced his body, doing this three times.

The people of the Sunan narrated it likewise, from the hadith of 'Uqayl, with the same wording [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5017); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5056); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3402); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10624); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3875)].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The reason for its revelation has already been mentioned. 'Ikrima said: When the Jews said, "We worship 'Uzayr, the son of Allah," and the Christians said, "We worship the Messiah, the son of Allah," and the Magians said, "We worship the sun and the moon," and the polytheists said, "We worship idols," Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾.

That is, He is the One, the Unique, who has no equal, no minister, no rival, no likeness and no peer. This term is not applied in affirmation to anyone except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because He is perfect in all His attributes and actions.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge﴾. 'Ikrima related from Ibn 'Abbas: it means the One to whom creatures turn in their needs and requests.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas: He is the Lord whose lordship is perfect, the Noble whose nobility is perfect, the Great whose greatness is perfect, the Forbearing whose forbearance is perfect, the Knowing whose knowledge is perfect, and the Wise whose wisdom is perfect; He is the One who is perfect in every kind of nobility and lordship. He is Allah, glory be to Him. This is His attribute, which befits none but Him; He has no equal, and there is nothing like unto Him. Glory be to Allah, the One, the Subduer.

Al-A'mash related from Shaqiq, from Abu Wa'il: al-Samad is the Lord whose lordship has reached its end. 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud related the same from Ibn Mas'ud.

Malik related from Zayd ibn Aslam: al-Samad is the Lord. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He is the One who remains after His creation. Al-Hasan also said: al-Samad is the Living, the Self-Subsisting, who has no cessation. 'Ikrima said: al-Samad is the One from whom nothing emerges and who is not fed.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: He is the One who has not begotten and has not been begotten; it seems he made what follows it an explanation of it, which is His saying: ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten﴾, and this is a fine explanation. The hadith has already been mentioned from the narration of Ibn Jarir, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b concerning this, and it is explicit in it.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, 'Abd Allah ibn Buraida, 'Ikrima also, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: al-Samad is the One who has no hollow (jawf).

Sufyan related from Mansur, from Mujahid: al-Samad is the solid one (al-musmat) who has no hollow.

Al-Sha'bi said: He is the One who does not eat food nor drink drink.

'Abd Allah ibn Buraida also said: al-Samad is a light that shines brilliantly.

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi and al-Tabarani related all of this and transmitted it, and likewise Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir related most of it with its chains, and said:

Al-'Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me; Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Rumi narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id, the guide of al-A'mash; Salih ibn Hayyan narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraida, from his father, who said, "I do not know except that he raised it (to the Prophet)": al-Samad is the One who has no hollow.

This is very strange (gharib), and the sound report is that it is halted (mawquf) at 'Abd Allah ibn Buraida.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani, in his book "al-Sunna", after citing many of these sayings in the interpretation of "al-Samad", said: "All of these are sound, and they are attributes of our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. He is the One to whom one turns in needs, He is the One whose nobility has reached its end, He is the Samad who has no hollow, who neither eats nor drinks, and who remains after His creation." Al-Bayhaqi said similar to this [also]. [Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya has elaborated greatly on the meaning of al-Samad in al-Fatawa (17/214).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, nor an equal.﴾ That is: He has no son, no father, and no consort.

Mujahid said: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ means: He has no consort.

Likewise is what Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have a son when He has no consort and He created all things?﴾ [al-An'am: 101] That is, He is the Owner and Creator of all things, so how could He have among His creation any equal who rivals Him, or any relative who draws near to Him? He is exalted, sanctified and far above that.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something monstrous. The heavens are almost rent from it, and the earth split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is no one in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them with [full] enumeration. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone.﴾ [Maryam: 88-95]

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants. They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26-27]

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a lineage. But the jinn have known that they will be brought [to account]. Exalted is Allah above what they describe.﴾ [as-Saffat: 158-159]

And in the Sahih, Sahih al-Bukhari: "No one is more patient with harm he hears than Allah. They attribute to Him a son, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6099), from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: The son of Adam denies Me, though he has no right to do so, and he reviles Me, though he has no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying: He will not bring me back as He originated me; and the first creation is not easier for Me than its return. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying: Allah has taken a son. And I am the One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Me."

He also narrated it through the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, in a marfu' report with the same wording. Al-Bukhari transmitted both of these chains alone.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4974) and no. (4975).]]

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Ikhlas".

**Tafsir of Surah Al-Ikhlas** (the Exegesis of Surah Al-Ikhlas, "Sincerity")

It is Meccan.

**Mention of the reason for its revelation and its virtue** [In M and A: "وفضلها", "and its virtue"]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'd Muhammad ibn Maysar al-Saghani narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated to us, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Muhammad, describe your Lord to us (inscribe your Lord's lineage for us)." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent.﴾ [Al-Musnad (5/133).]

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir also narrated it similarly, from Ahmad ibn Mani' (Ibn Jarir added: and Mahmud ibn Khidash), from Abu Sa'd Muhammad ibn Maysar with this chain. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3364, and Tafsir al-Tabari (30/221, 223).] Ibn Jarir and al-Tirmidhi added: He said: "The Samad is the One who neither begets nor is begotten, because everything that is begotten will certainly die, and everything that dies will certainly be inherited, whereas Allah, may His majesty be exalted, neither dies nor is inherited. ﴿Nor is there to Him any equivalent﴾ means: there is no likeness to Him, no equal, and there is nothing like Him."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from the hadith of Abu Sa'd [in M and A: "Sa'id"] Muhammad ibn Maysar, with this chain. Then al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abd ibn Humayd, from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, and he mentioned it as mursal (with the companion omitted), without saying "akhbarana" (he informed us). Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is more authentic than the hadith of Abu Sa'd." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3365.]

**Another hadith with the same meaning:** Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Suraij [in A: "Shurayh"] ibn Yunus narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Mujalid narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir: that a Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Describe your Lord to us." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ to the end of it. Its isnad (chain of narration) is close [in M: "its isnad is close"]. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (4/38-39) and Tafsir al-Tabari (30/221). Mujalid is weak in his narration from al-Sha'bi from Jabir.]

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Muhammad ibn Awf, from Suraij [in A: "Shurayh"], and mentioned it. Many of the early scholars narrated it as mursal.

Ubayd ibn Ishaq al-Attar narrated from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'Describe your Lord to us,' and so this surah was revealed: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾" Al-Tabarani said: "al-Firyabi and others narrated it from Qays, from Abu 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il, as mursal." [Al-Tayalisi narrated it from Qays, from Asim, from Abu Wa'il, as mursal, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. 89.]

Then al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman al-Ta'ifi, from al-Waza' ibn Nafi', from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Everything has a lineage, and the lineage of Allah is: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ And the Samad is not hollow." [In M and A, the text includes "لَيْسَ بِأَجْوَفَ" as an addition from A.] [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 3423, in Majma' al-Bahrayn, through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafi', from 'Ali ibn Thabit, from al-Waza', from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah with this (wording). He said: "It is not narrated from Abu Hurairah except through this chain; 'Abd al-Rahman alone narrated it."]

**Another hadith on its virtue:** Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad [al-Dhuhli] narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Amr informed us, from Ibn Abi Hilal, that Abu al-Rijal Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to him, from his mother 'Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman (who was in the care of 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ), from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet ﷺ sent a man as commander of a expedition (sariyyah), and he used to recite for his companions in their prayers, and he would end with ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ When they returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Ask him why he does that." So they asked him, and he said: "Because it is the attribute of the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Inform him that Allah, the Exalted, loves him."

Al-Bukhari narrated it thus in his book "al-Tawhid." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7375.] Some people omit the mention of "Muhammad al-Dhuhli" and make it from his narration from Ahmad ibn Salih. Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Wahb, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, with this. [Sahih Muslim, no. 813, and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/170).]

**Another hadith:** Al-Bukhari said in the Book of Prayer: "'Ubayd Allah [in A: "Abd Allah"] narrated from Thabit, from Anas, who said: A man from the Ansar used to lead them in prayer at the Mosque of Quba. Whenever he began a surah he would recite to them in the prayer, of what he recited, he would begin with ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ until he finished it, then he would recite another surah with it, and he would do this in every rak'ah. His companions spoke to him and said: 'You begin with this surah, then you do not seem to think it suffices you until you recite another with it. Either recite it, or leave it and recite another.' He said: 'I will not leave it. If you wish me to lead you with it, I will do so, and if you dislike it, I will leave you.' They thought he was among the best of them, and they disliked that anyone other than him should lead them. When the Prophet ﷺ came to them, they informed him of the matter. He said: 'O so-and-so, what prevents you from doing what your companions command you, and what compels you to persist in this surah in every rak'ah?' He said: 'I love it.' He said: 'Your love for it has admitted you into Paradise.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 774.]

Thus al-Bukhari narrated it as a mu'allaq (a hadith cited without its full chain), stated with certainty. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Jami', from al-Bukhari, from Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, and he mentioned it with its chain, the same, identically. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2901.] Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (singular) from the hadith of Ubayd Allah, from Thabit." He said: "Mubarak ibn Fadalah also narrated from Thabit, from Anas, that a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I love this surah: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾' He said: 'Indeed your love for it has admitted you into Paradise.'"

What al-Tirmidhi cited without a chain, Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad as connected (muttasil), so he said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I love this surah: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your love for it [in M: "Indeed your love"] has admitted you into Paradise." [Al-Musnad (3/141).]

**A hadith on its being equal to a third of the Qur'an:** Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il narrated to us, Malik narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah, from his father, from Abu Sa'id, that a man heard another man reciting ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ repeatedly. When morning came, he went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, as though the man belittled it. The Prophet ﷺ [in M: "the Messenger of Allah"] said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is indeed equal to a third of the Qur'an." Isma'il ibn Ja'far added, from Malik, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah, from his father, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "My brother Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man informed me, from the Prophet ﷺ." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7374.]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf and al-Qa'nabi. Abu Dawud narrated it from al-Qa'nabi, and al-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, all from Malik, with this chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 5013 and 6643; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1461; and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/171).] The hadith of Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man was also recorded by al-Nasa'i through two routes, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Malik, with this chain. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. 8029 and 10536.]

**Another hadith:** Al-Bukhari said: Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Ibrahim and al-Dahhak al-Mashriqi narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: "Is one of you unable to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night?" That was difficult for them, and they said: "Which of us can manage that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Allah, the One, the Samad, is a third of the Qur'an." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5015.]

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Nakha'i and al-Dahhak ibn Shurahbil al-Hamdani al-Mashriqi, both from Abu Sa'id. Al-Qarabiri said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim, the scribe of Abu Abd Allah [al-Bukhari], say: Abu Abd Allah al-Bukhari said: "From Ibrahim it is mursal (its link is broken), and from al-Dahhak it is musnad (connected)." [Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (9/60): "The meaning is that the narration of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i from Abu Sa'id is munqati' (broken), and al-Dahhak's narration from him is muttasil (connected)."]

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man spent the whole night reciting ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾. This was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is equal to half of the Qur'an, or a third of it." [Al-Musnad (3/15).]

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Huyayy ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, that Abu Ayyub al-Ansari was in a gathering, saying: "Is none of you able to stand in prayer for a third of the Qur'an every night?" They said: "Is anyone able to do that?" He said: "Indeed, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ is a third of the Qur'an." Then the Prophet ﷺ came while he was listening to Abu Ayyub, and he said: "Abu Ayyub has spoken the truth." [Al-Musnad (2/173).]

**Another hadith:** Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yazid ibn Kaysan narrated to us, Abu Hazim informed me, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Gather together, for I will recite to you a third of the Qur'an." So whoever gathered gathered, then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out and recited ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, then went back in. Some of us said to others: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I will recite to you a third of the Qur'an.' I think this is news that came from heaven." Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out and said: "I said: 'I will recite to you a third of the Qur'an.' Indeed, it [this surah] is equal to a third of the Qur'an."

Muslim narrated it likewise in his Sahih, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, with this chain. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2900, and Sahih Muslim, no. 812.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib." The name of Abu Hazim is Salman.

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Za'idah ibn Qudamah, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym [in A: "ibn Khaythum"], from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from a woman of the Ansar, from Abu Ayyub, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Is one of you unable to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night? For whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ in a night, has indeed recited a third of the Qur'an that night."

This is a hadith with a nine-narrator chain (tusa'i al-isnad) from Imam Ahmad. It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, both from Muhammad ibn Bashshar Bundar (in one manuscript: "Yasar"). Al-Tirmidhi added Qutayba, and both of them narrated it from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, with it. Thus it becomes a ten-narrator chain (ushari) for the two of them. In al-Tirmidhi's narration it reads: "from the wife of Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ayyub," with it [and he graded it hasan]. Then he said: "And on this subject there are reports from Abu al-Darda', Abu Sa'id, Qatada ibn al-Nu'man, Abu Hurayra, Anas, Ibn Umar and Abu Mas'ud." He said: "This is a hasan (sound-good) hadith, and we do not know anyone who narrated this hadith better than the narration of Za'ida." Israil and al-Fudayl ibn Iyad followed him in his narration. Shu'ba and others of the trustworthy narrators related this hadith from Mansur, and they disagreed about it (idtarabu fihi).

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, or a man from the Ansar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ has recited a third of the Qur'an." [Musnad, 5/141.]

Al-Nasa'i related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla," from the hadith of Hushaym, from Husayn, from Ibn Abi Layla, with it. But in his narration the name Hilal ibn Yasaf does not appear. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10521.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Qays [in one manuscript: "Ishaq"], from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abu Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an." [Musnad, 4/122.]

Ibn Majah related it in the same way, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi, from Waki, with it. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3789.] Al-Nasa'i related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla" from various other routes, from Amr ibn Maymun, both as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) and as a mawquf (ending with a companion). [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra nos. 10529, 10525, 10528.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Bahz narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Abi al-Samit narrated to us [in one manuscript: "Bakr ibn Abi al-Simt"], Qatada narrated to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talha, from Abu al-Darda', that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Is one of you incapable of reciting a third of the Qur'an every day?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are weaker than that and less able." He said: "Indeed Allah divided the Qur'an into three parts, and ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ is a third of the Qur'an." [Musnad, 1/447; Sahih Muslim no. 811; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10537.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Umayya ibn Khalid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muslim, the nephew of Ibn Shihab, narrated to us, from his paternal uncle al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, who is Ibn Awf, from his mother, who was Umm Kulthum bint Uqba [in one manuscript: "Utba"] ibn Abi Mu'ayt, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an."

Likewise al-Nasa'i related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla," from Amr ibn Ali, from Umayya ibn Khalid, with it. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10531.] Then he related it through the route of Malik, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, as his own statement (qawlahu, i.e., not traced to the Prophet ﷺ). [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10533.] Al-Nasa'i also related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla" from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Harith ibn al-Fudayl al-Ansari, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman: that a group of the companions of Muhammad ﷺ told him from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an for whoever prays with it." [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10532.]

Another hadith on the reward of reciting it bringing Paradise: Imam Malik ibn Anas said, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ubayd ibn Hunayn, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: "I came along with the Prophet ﷺ, and he heard a man reciting ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Wajabat' (it is obligatory)." I said: "And what is obligatory?" He said: "Paradise." [Muwatta, 2/208; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2897; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 2/171.]

Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Malik. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib (a sound-good hadith that is also gharib, meaning transmitted through a single route); we do not know it except from the hadith of Malik."

And the hadith previously mentioned has already passed: "Your love for it has caused you to enter Paradise."

A hadith on repeating its recitation: The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Qutan ibn Nusayr narrated to us, Isa ibn Maymun al-Qurashi narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqashi narrated to us, from Anas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Can none of you manage to recite ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ three times in a night? For indeed it equals a third of the Qur'an." [Musnad Abi Ya'la, 8/150. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/147): "In its chain is Ubays, who is matruk (abandoned)."]

This chain is weak. A better one than it is another hadith. Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad said:

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from Usayd ibn Abi Usayd, from Mu'adh ibn Abd Allah ibn Khubayb, from his father, who said: A heavy rain and darkness afflicted us, so we waited for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to lead us in prayer. He came out, took my hand, and said: "Say." I was silent. He said: "Say." I said: "What should I say?" He said: "Say ﴿He is Allah, the One﴾ and the two protectors (al-Mu'awwidhatayn), when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, three times, and they will suffice you every day twice."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, with it. [Zawa'id al-Musnad, 5/312; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 5082; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3575; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 8/250.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib from this route." Al-Nasa'i related it through another route, from Mu'adh ibn Abd Allah ibn Khubayb, from his father, from Uqba ibn Amir, and mentioned it [with its wording: "it will suffice you for everything"]. [Sunan al-Nasa'i, 8/251.]

Another hadith on the same subject: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, al-Khalil ibn Murra narrated to me, from al-Azhar ibn Abd Allah, from Tamim al-Dari, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah, alone, the One, the Eternal Refuge (Samad), who has not taken a consort or a son, and to whom no one is equal,' ten times, will have written for him forty million good deeds."

Ahmad alone related it. Al-Khalil ibn Murra was declared weak by al-Bukhari and others, in the sense of his being weak in narration (bi-murra).

Another hadith: Ahmad also said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Zabban ibn Fa'id narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ until he finishes it, ten times, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise." Umar said: "Then we will have many, O Messenger of Allah." He ﷺ said: "Allah is greater and better." Ahmad alone related it. [Musnad, 3/437.]

Abu Muhammad al-Darimi related it in his Musnad, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Haywa narrated to us, Abu Uqayl Zahra ibn Ma'bad narrated to us (al-Darimi said: "He was among the abdal (a class of saints)") that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ ten times, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise; whoever recites it twenty times, Allah will build for him two palaces in Paradise; and whoever recites it thirty times, Allah will build for him three palaces in Paradise." Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Then our palaces will be many!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah is wider than that." [Sunan al-Darimi no. 3429.] This is a mursal (a report where the Successor omits the Companion) of good quality.

Another hadith: The hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us, Nuh ibn Qays narrated to me, Muhammad al-Attar informed me, Umm Kathir al-Ansariyya informed me, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ fifty times, Allah will forgive him the sins of fifty years." [Al-Darimi related it in his Sunan no. 3438: Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us in the same wording.] Its chain is weak.

Another hadith: Abu Ya'la said: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites in a day ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ two hundred times, Allah will record for him one thousand five hundred good deeds, unless he has a debt." [Musnad Abi Ya'la, 6/103.] Its chain is weak; Hatim ibn Maymun was declared weak by al-Bukhari and others. al-Tirmidhi related it from Muhammad ibn Marzuq al-Basri, from Hatim ibn Maymun, with it, and its wording is: "Whoever recites every day two hundred times ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, the sins of fifty years will be erased from him, unless he has a debt."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "With this same chain, from the Prophet ﷺ, it is also related that he said: 'Whoever wants to sleep on his bed, and sleeps on his right side, then recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ one hundred times, then on the Day of Resurrection the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will say to him: O My servant, enter Paradise on your right side.'" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2898.] Then he said: "Gharib from the hadith of Thabit, and it has been related through another route from him."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Sahl ibn Bahr narrated to us, Habban ibn Aghlab narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ two hundred times, Allah will remove from him the sins of two hundred years." [Also related by Ibn al-Darис in Fada'il al-Qur'an no. 267, and al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad 6/187, through al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Thabit, with it.] Then he said: "We do not know anyone who related it from Thabit except al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far and al-Aghlab ibn Tamim, and both are close to each other in poor memorization."

Another hadith on supplicating with the names it contains: Al-Nasa'i said, in his explanation of it: Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to me, Abd Allah ibn Buraydah narrated to us, from his father: that he entered the mosque with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there was a man praying and supplicating, saying: "O Allah, I ask You, by my testifying that there is no god but You, the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad), who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, he has asked Him by His Greatest Name, which when He is asked by it He gives, and when He is called upon by it He answers." [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, as in Tuhfat al-Ashraf of al-Mizzi, 2/90.]

It has been related by the rest of the authors of the Sunan through various routes, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, with it. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1493; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3475; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3857.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

Another hadith on reciting it ten times after the obligatory prayer: The hafiz Abu Ya'la [al-Mawsili] [added from one manuscript] said: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Bishr ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Umar ibn Nabhan [in manuscripts M, A and H: "Umar ibn Shaybān"], from Abu Shaddad, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three things, whoever comes with them along with faith, may enter by whichever gate of Paradise he wishes, and be married to the Huris (al-Hur al-'Iyn) wherever he wishes: whoever pardons the one who killed him, pays a hidden debt, and recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ ten times after every obligatory prayer." He said: Abu Bakr said: "Or one of them, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Or one of them." [Musnad Abi Ya'la, 3/332. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/102): "In it is Umar ibn Nabhan, who is matruk."]

A hadith on reciting it upon entering the house: The memorizer of hadith (al-Hafiz) Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sarraj al-'Askari narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Faraj narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Zibriqan narrated to us, from Marwan ibn Salim, from Abu Zur'a ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ when he enters his house, it removes poverty from the people of that house and from the neighbours." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/340).] Its isnad (chain of narration) is weak.

A hadith on frequently reciting it in all circumstances: The memorizer Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Musayyabi narrated to us; Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Tabuk, and the sun rose with a light, a radiance and a brightness such as we had not seen it rise with before. Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and [he] said: 'O Jibril, why do I see the sun rise today with a light, brightness and radiance such as I have not seen it rise with in the past?' He said: 'That is because Mu'awiya ibn Mu'awiya al-Laythi died in Medina today, so Allah sent to him seventy thousand angels who pray over him.' He said: 'And why is that?' He said: 'He used to frequently recite: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, at night and by day, while walking, standing and sitting. Would you like, O Messenger of Allah, that I fold the earth for you so that you may pray over him?' He said: 'Yes.' So he prayed over him."

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi also narrated it in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwa" by way of Yazid ibn Harun, from al-'Ala' Abu Muhammad [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/256) and Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (5/245)]. He is accused of fabrication (wad'), so Allah knows best.

Another route: Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Shami Abu 'Abd Allah narrated to us; 'Uthman ibn al-Haytham, the muezzin of the congregational mosque in Basra (in my presence), narrated to us, from Mahmud Abu 'Abd Allah [in the original manuscript of Musnad Abi Ya'la it reads "Mahmud ibn 'Abd Allah", but here it reads "Mahmud Abi 'Abd Allah", as you see; the correct reading is "Mahbub ibn Hilal", as in the narration of al-Bayhaqi, Allah knows best], from 'Ata' ibn Abi Maymuna, from Anas, who said: Jibril descended upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Mu'awiya ibn Mu'awiya al-Laythi has died; would you like to pray over him?" He said: "Yes." So he struck the earth with his wing, and no tree or hillock remained without being lowered. He raised his bier and looked at him, then he pronounced takbir over him, with behind him two rows of angels, each row seventy thousand angels. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, by what did he attain this rank with Allah, the Exalted?" He said: "By his love for it: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, and his recitation of it while walking, coming, standing and sitting, and in every state." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/258).]

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the narration of 'Uthman ibn al-Haytham the muezzin, from Mahbub ibn Hilal, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Maymuna, from Anas, and so on. This is the correct version [Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (5/246); Ibn al-Durays narrated it in "Fada'il al-Qur'an" under no. 272, by way of Mahbub ibn Hilal; the author cited it in al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya from al-Bayhaqi's narration (5/14) and said: "Munkar from this route"]. Mahbub ibn Hilal: Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: "Not well known" [al-Jarh wa'l-Ta'dil by Ibn Abi Hatim (8/389)]. This has been narrated by other routes, which we have omitted for brevity, and all of them are weak.

Another hadith on its merit together with the two refuges (al-Mu'awwidhatayn): The Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us; Mu'adh ibn Rifa'a narrated to us; 'Ali ibn Yazid narrated to me, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, who said: I met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I took the initiative, took his hand and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by what is the believer saved?" He said: "O 'Uqba, guard your tongue, let your house suffice you, and weep over your sin." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met me again, took the initiative, took my hand and said: "O 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, shall I not teach you the best three surahs revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Great Qur'an?" I said: "Yes, may Allah make me your ransom." He said: He taught me: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, and ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾. Then he said: "O 'Uqba, do not forget them, and do not sleep a night until you have recited them." He said: I have not forgotten them since he said: "Do not forget them," and I have never spent a night without reciting them. 'Uqba said: Then I met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), took the initiative, took his hand and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me of the most virtuous deeds." He said: "O 'Uqba, join ties with the one who cuts you off, give to the one who deprives you, and forgive the one who wrongs you." [Al-Musnad (4/148).]

Al-Tirmidhi narrated part of it in "al-Zuhd", from the hadith of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, and said: "This is a hasan hadith" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2406)]. Its isnad includes 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, 'Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim, all of whom are weak. Ibn Hibban said of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr: "He narrates fabricated reports from reliable narrators, and when he narrates from 'Ali ibn Yazid he brings forth abominations; and when a report's isnad contains 'Ubayd Allah, 'Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim (Abu 'Abd al-Rahman), that report is nothing but what their hands have produced." [Note on the text of Ibn Hibban.] Ahmad narrated it by another route:

Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Usayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khath'ami, from Furwa ibn Mujahid al-Lakhmi, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned the like of it exactly. Ahmad alone narrated it [Al-Musnad (4/158)].

Another hadith on seeking healing with them: Al-Bukhari said: Qutayba narrated to us; al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha, that the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he went to his bed every night, joined his palms, then blew into them and recited in them: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, and ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾; then he would wipe with them as much of his body as he could, beginning with his head and face and what faced his body, doing this three times.

The people of the Sunan narrated it likewise, from the hadith of 'Uqayl, with the same wording [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5017); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5056); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3402); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10624); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3875)].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The reason for its revelation has already been mentioned. 'Ikrima said: When the Jews said, "We worship 'Uzayr, the son of Allah," and the Christians said, "We worship the Messiah, the son of Allah," and the Magians said, "We worship the sun and the moon," and the polytheists said, "We worship idols," Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾.

That is, He is the One, the Unique, who has no equal, no minister, no rival, no likeness and no peer. This term is not applied in affirmation to anyone except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because He is perfect in all His attributes and actions.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge﴾. 'Ikrima related from Ibn 'Abbas: it means the One to whom creatures turn in their needs and requests.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas: He is the Lord whose lordship is perfect, the Noble whose nobility is perfect, the Great whose greatness is perfect, the Forbearing whose forbearance is perfect, the Knowing whose knowledge is perfect, and the Wise whose wisdom is perfect; He is the One who is perfect in every kind of nobility and lordship. He is Allah, glory be to Him. This is His attribute, which befits none but Him; He has no equal, and there is nothing like unto Him. Glory be to Allah, the One, the Subduer.

Al-A'mash related from Shaqiq, from Abu Wa'il: al-Samad is the Lord whose lordship has reached its end. 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud related the same from Ibn Mas'ud.

Malik related from Zayd ibn Aslam: al-Samad is the Lord. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He is the One who remains after His creation. Al-Hasan also said: al-Samad is the Living, the Self-Subsisting, who has no cessation. 'Ikrima said: al-Samad is the One from whom nothing emerges and who is not fed.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: He is the One who has not begotten and has not been begotten; it seems he made what follows it an explanation of it, which is His saying: ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten﴾, and this is a fine explanation. The hadith has already been mentioned from the narration of Ibn Jarir, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b concerning this, and it is explicit in it.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, 'Abd Allah ibn Buraida, 'Ikrima also, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: al-Samad is the One who has no hollow (jawf).

Sufyan related from Mansur, from Mujahid: al-Samad is the solid one (al-musmat) who has no hollow.

Al-Sha'bi said: He is the One who does not eat food nor drink drink.

'Abd Allah ibn Buraida also said: al-Samad is a light that shines brilliantly.

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi and al-Tabarani related all of this and transmitted it, and likewise Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir related most of it with its chains, and said:

Al-'Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me; Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Rumi narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id, the guide of al-A'mash; Salih ibn Hayyan narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraida, from his father, who said, "I do not know except that he raised it (to the Prophet)": al-Samad is the One who has no hollow.

This is very strange (gharib), and the sound report is that it is halted (mawquf) at 'Abd Allah ibn Buraida.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani, in his book "al-Sunna", after citing many of these sayings in the interpretation of "al-Samad", said: "All of these are sound, and they are attributes of our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. He is the One to whom one turns in needs, He is the One whose nobility has reached its end, He is the Samad who has no hollow, who neither eats nor drinks, and who remains after His creation." Al-Bayhaqi said similar to this [also]. [Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya has elaborated greatly on the meaning of al-Samad in al-Fatawa (17/214).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, nor an equal.﴾ That is: He has no son, no father, and no consort.

Mujahid said: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ means: He has no consort.

Likewise is what Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have a son when He has no consort and He created all things?﴾ [al-An'am: 101] That is, He is the Owner and Creator of all things, so how could He have among His creation any equal who rivals Him, or any relative who draws near to Him? He is exalted, sanctified and far above that.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something monstrous. The heavens are almost rent from it, and the earth split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is no one in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them with [full] enumeration. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone.﴾ [Maryam: 88-95]

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants. They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26-27]

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a lineage. But the jinn have known that they will be brought [to account]. Exalted is Allah above what they describe.﴾ [as-Saffat: 158-159]

And in the Sahih, Sahih al-Bukhari: "No one is more patient with harm he hears than Allah. They attribute to Him a son, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6099), from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: The son of Adam denies Me, though he has no right to do so, and he reviles Me, though he has no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying: He will not bring me back as He originated me; and the first creation is not easier for Me than its return. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying: Allah has taken a son. And I am the One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Me."

He also narrated it through the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, in a marfu' report with the same wording. Al-Bukhari transmitted both of these chains alone.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4974) and no. (4975).]]

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Ikhlas".
